summary: A 1917 state fire tower on Sand Mountain in Union County, replaced in 1950 by an 80-ft Aermotor moved from Hartley; registered but in poor condition, access prohibited in 2022.

facts.design: 80-ft Aermotor moved in from Eastville (Hartley) in 1950; it replaced an original 60-ft steel Aermotor of 1917
facts.status_note: Standing in very poor condition at a June 2022 visit; the district was awaiting funding to remove it

access.note: 2022 visit report says access to the tower is prohibited; a large communications tower stands next to the site

visit.trail_note: Access to the tower is prohibited according to the June 2022 visit report

events.note: Steel Aermotor observation tower erected August and September 1917 on Sand Mountain, bought from the Aermotor Company of Chicago; a line about four miles long was built from the Forest House to the tower in 1918
Steel Aermotor tower first built at the Hartley (Eastville) site in Union County; later moved to Sand Mountain
Original 1917 tower replaced by an 80-ft Aermotor moved in from Eastville (Hartley); the Union County II site entry gives 1951
Registered September 16, 2008 as US 467, PA 296 (Sand Mountain Tower Site, Union County II)
June 4, 2022 visit report: very poor condition, unstaffed, access prohibited, district awaiting funding to remove the tower

corrections.why: The NHLR entry describes the standing 1950 tower as an 80-ft Aermotor (about 24.4 m). No source checked supports 27.4 m (90 ft).

corrections.proposed: 1917 built (original 60-ft steel Aermotor); 1950 replaced (80-ft Aermotor moved in from Hartley/Eastville)
corrections.why: The 1950 date is when the current tower was installed. The site's first tower was built in 1917, as the NHLR description and the 1917 contract both show.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR Built field gives 1950, which is the current tower's install date. The NHLR description and the 1917 state records date the first tower on the site to 1917.
The NHLR and the Hartley site entry both give 1950 for the move. The Union County II entry gives 1951. I have used 1950 and noted the other.
A 1917 contract describes a sixty-three-foot tower. A 1917 report and the NHLR description give sixty feet.

The FFLOS Union County II entry (US 467) has nearly the same coordinates as the NHLR record (US 1253), so both describe the same ridge. The separate FFLOS Union County I entry (US 468) is a different site and was not checked.

sources.title: Sand Mountain Tower Site (Union County II)

notes_for_editor: Replacement year conflicts (1950 NHLR and Hartley entry vs 1951 FFLOS Union II). Height conflicts (60 ft and 63 ft for the 1917 tower; record's 27.4 m is not supported by any source checked). Staffing and access rest on a single 2022 visit report, so treat them as dated. The weebly Sand Mountain page ends with a stray 'Removed' label that I could not place, so I did not use it. The 1917 tower's fate after its 1950 replacement is not documented. Anyplaceamerica topo page returned 403 and was not read.
